questions.q: What is Tableau, at its core?
options: A data visualization and business intelligence platform that turns connected data into interactive charts and dashboards
A relational database engine, like SQL Server
A programming language for building web applications
A spreadsheet application that replaces Excel
questions.explain: Tableau connects to data and turns it into interactive visualizations and dashboards — it solves the same core problem as Power BI, with a different tool and philosophy.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does this catalog teach both Power BI and Tableau?
options: A large number of real BI Developer and Data Analyst job postings ask for Tableau specifically, often instead of or alongside Power BI, so knowing both widens your job search
Power BI and Tableau are actually the same product with different names
Tableau has replaced Power BI in the market entirely
This course only teaches Tableau; Power BI is unrelated
questions.explain: Tableau and Power BI have real, distinct market share — a meaningful number of postings specifically ask for Tableau, so knowing both tools makes you employable at a wider range of companies.

questions.q: In the Tableau Desktop workspace, what does the Data pane show?
options: Every field from your connected data source, split into Dimensions and Measures
A list of every dashboard you've ever published
The SQL query Tableau generated behind the scenes
A history of every chart type you've used
questions.explain: The Data pane lists every field from the connected data source, already split into Dimensions and Measures — the split Lesson 5 covers in depth.

questions.q: What does this course assume you already know coming in, and how does that change how SQL-adjacent Tableau topics (like joins or filtering) are taught?
options: It assumes you already know SQL from T-SQL Development, so lessons teach how those already-familiar concepts behave specifically inside Tableau, not from scratch
It assumes no prior knowledge of anything, including basic computer use
It assumes you've already used Tableau professionally for years
It assumes you know Python but not SQL
questions.explain: This course builds on the SQL knowledge from T-SQL Development — it teaches how already-known concepts behave inside Tableau's specific engine, rather than re-teaching SQL fundamentals from zero.

questions.q: What dataset does the workspace screenshot in this lesson use, and why does that matter for the rest of the course?
options: Sample Superstore — the same dataset Lesson 3 has you download, and one this course returns to throughout Chapters 1-13
AdventureWorks2012 — the same database used in the T-SQL Development course
A dataset invented specifically for this screenshot, used nowhere else in the course
The screenshot doesn't use any real dataset
questions.explain: The screenshot uses Tableau's own Sample Superstore dataset, which Lesson 3 has you download directly and which recurs throughout much of this course.
